12.1d — Grid/Symmetry Jam: Playtest

The 10.1d ritual, one last time — with grid-specific tells to watch. Symmetry games are the most data-friendly jam of the year: every move is an index, every death has a cell address, every hesitation happens AT a coordinate.

Playtest ~45 min

Three rounds, same contracts: watch silently (2.4), record on a beat table, ONE fix, verify, revert on failure. The grid-specific tells:

  • The orientation stall: tester presses up and the cursor moves a direction they did not expect. Your y-flip (12.1c sign) or their mental model? (If two testers stall the same way, it is YOUR sign.)
  • The symmetry question: "wait, are we playing the same game?" — asked with delight means your fairness reads; asked with confusion means the mirror is invisible (RENDER it)
  • The cell ambiguity: the tester miscounts a gap or misreads adjacency. Grids promise precision — visual gaps or soft colors break the promise
  • Tie-break feels: the deadlock you defined — did the tester experience it as fair? If they protest the SAME tie twice, the rule loses (change it or make it visible)

Data, grid edition: log the CELL of every death and every hesitation (column,row). Your playtest.csv gains coordinates — and a heatmap of the board falls out for free: which cells kill, which cells teach?

Bug Hunt: Playtest-day decisions

  1. A tester suggests adding a mechanic mid-run. Write it down — but why is "put it in the NEXT jam" almost always right in the last jam's last build day (10.1e freeze rules apply tomorrow)?
  2. Your fix made the board readable but killed the difficulty. Revert or redesign? Which question decides (3.4: hard vs unclear — never fix both at once)?

Tinker: Close

  1. Update playtest.csv; commit: "12.1d: playtest + fix verified".
  2. Build + test the BUILD (freeze discipline — showcase is 12.1e).

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Watch for the four grid tells and diagnose each
  • Log deaths/hesitations with cell coordinates
  • Apply one fix, verify, revert on failure
  • Leave with a tested build for showcase day
